findings.overloaded: Overloaded: {{nodeNames}} runs at {{utilizationPct}}% and is bound by {{boundBy}} at a capacity of {{capacity}} req/s; {{dropped}} req/s are dropped. Add instances, shard it, or cut the traffic.
findings.saturated: Close to the limit: {{nodeNames}} runs at {{utilizationPct}}%, bound by {{boundBy}} at a capacity of {{capacity}} req/s. The queue will grow at peak.
findings.retry-storm: Retry storm: the model did not converge — retries add load faster than the system drains it. Reduce the retry count, add backoff and a circuit breaker.
findings.retry-amplification: Retries inflate the load: {{nodeNames}} receives {{amplificationPct}}% more requests because of repeats. Raise the timeout or enable exponential backoff.
findings.spof: Single point of failure: {{nodeNames}} has no standby — losing it breaks the whole request path. Add a second replica or a second zone.
findings.hot-key: Hot key: {{nodeNames}} takes {{hotKeyRps}} req/s on a single shard whose capacity is {{perShardCapacity}} req/s. Spread the key out or put a local cache in front.
findings.client-direct-to-store: The client talks to the store directly ({{nodeNames}}). Put a service or a gateway in between — otherwise there is no authorization, no limits and no cache.
findings.retry-without-idempotency: Retries without idempotency: {{retries}} retries are configured, but the operation is not idempotent ({{nodeNames}}). A retry creates a duplicate — add an idempotency key.
findings.backlog-growing: The backlog grows: the producer emits {{producerRps}} msg/s while the consumer drains {{consumerCapacity}} msg/s — the lag adds {{growthPerSec}} msg/s. Add consumers or partitions.
findings.read-heavy-without-cache: Reads without a cache: {{nodeNames}} serves {{readRps}} reads/s at {{utilizationPct}}% utilization. A cache in front of the store removes most of that load.
findings.egress-dominates: Traffic dominates the bill: egress is {{sharePct}}% of the cost ({{egressCost}} $/mo). Enable a CDN, compress responses, or keep the traffic inside the region.
findings.unmodelled: No model: {{nodeNames}} is not simulated yet — its capacity and latency are excluded from the estimate.
findings.anomaly-stale-read: Stale reads: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}% of reads) return outdated data because of replica lag ({{nodeNames}}). Read from the primary where freshness matters.
findings.anomaly-read-your-writes: The user does not see their own write: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) hit a replica before the change lands ({{nodeNames}}). Pin the session to the primary.
findings.anomaly-lost-update: Lost updates: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}% of writes) overwrite each other ({{nodeNames}}). Use versions, CAS, or transactions instead of read-modify-write.
findings.anomaly-write-conflict: Write conflicts: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) edit the same key from different regions ({{nodeNames}}). Pin the key to one region or switch to CRDTs.
findings.anomaly-lost-write-lww: Writes are lost to last-write-wins: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) are silently discarded as losers ({{nodeNames}}). Change the conflict resolution strategy.
findings.anomaly-duplicate-processing: Duplicate processing: {{ratePerSec}} ops/s ({{sharePct}}%) are handled twice ({{nodeNames}}). At-least-once without idempotency causes double effects.
findings.unknown-component: Unknown block "{{type}}": it is not in the catalog and is excluded from the estimate.
findings.dangling-edge: Dangling edge: one of its ends points at a block that does not exist.
findings.no-entry-point: No entry point: add a client — without one there is no load to simulate.
findings.cycle-detected: Cycle in the scheme: {{size}} blocks call each other in a loop — latency there is approximated.
findings.unreachable-node: Unreachable block: {{nodeNames}} receives no traffic from any client.
findings.deep-sync-chain: Deep synchronous chain: {{depth}} hops in a row starting at {{nodeNames}}. Every hop multiplies latency and failure odds — move part of it off the request path.
